# parsec v5 — T1 (original skill) zero-shot baseline, v5_t1_e1

**Spec:** none written — this is a benchmark-isolation rebuild, not a new optimizer experiment (see "Why v5 exists" below)
**Agent model:** `claude-sonnet-4-6`
**Optimizer model:** none — **no optimization step**. v5_t1_e1 evaluates the original, unmodified PARSEC skill zero-shot; there is no seed/candidate/best/final lineage here, unlike `v4_t_e1`.
**Budget:** `num_trials: 5, max_usd: 50.0` per task (no optimizer budget — none was spent)
**Ledger:** [`results.json`](results.json), generated by [`../../../scripts/build_v5_t1_results_json.py`](../../../scripts/build_v5_t1_results_json.py) from the vendored [`source_v5_t1_e1.json`](source_v5_t1_e1.json)
**Heatmap:** [`../../../ui/heatmap_v5_t1_e1.html`](../../../ui/heatmap_v5_t1_e1.html)
**Recipes:** [`../../../recipes/v5/v5_t1_e1/`](../../../recipes/v5/v5_t1_e1/) (no `capevolve.yaml` — this was a harness sweep, not a `cap-evolve run` invocation; see that README)
**Artifacts:** [`../../../artifacts/v5/seed/`](../../../artifacts/v5/seed/) (one shared bundle, identical across all 68 tasks — nothing was optimized per-task)
**Per-task reports:** [`../../../reports/v5/v5_t1_e1/`](../../../reports/v5/v5_t1_e1/) (`<task>.md`, 68 files)
**Cost/time source:** [`cost_time/`](cost_time/) (`v5_t1_e1_results_table.md`)
**v5 vs. v4/h4:** see [`../../../reports/v5-vs-v4-h4-comparison.md`](../../../reports/v5-vs-v4-h4-comparison.md)

## Why v5 exists

v4's original 34-task set and h4's 30-task held-out set (`v4_t_e1`, `reports/v4/h4/`) were both
found, during this benchmark's setup, to have drifted from the task copies this repo's own
`v4_t4_e1`/`v4_t4_e2`/`h4_t1_e1`/`h4_t1_e3` tables were built against (different `golden.json`,
seeds, and `verify.py` in several tasks — one with a dated bug fix). Rather than reconcile that
lineage, v5 is a **from-scratch, physically isolated rebuild**: new task copies under a renamed
`bench-v5-` prefix, no shared code or content with any v4/h4 worktree, logic and parameters kept
identical to what was proven to work for v4/h4. `v5_t1_e1` is the first arm run against it: the
same T1 (original, unmodified) skill, zero-shot, 5 trials/task, now across **all 68** v5 tasks (not
just the 34 that have a v4 lineage) — the user's explicit call once it became clear the original 34
also differ from v4's own copies, to avoid introducing comparison bugs by only partially migrating.

## The one-line result

Mean reward **0.8885** across all 68 tasks, 0 errored trials anywhere, 36 tasks saturated at 1.0.
On the 55 tasks that match a prior arm by task id (34 matching v4's set, 21 matching h4's — see
"Matched comparison" below), v5_t1_e1 reads **above** both: +0.122 over the pooled matched mean. That
delta is **not a controlled A/B** — see the caveat in the next section — so it's reported as an
orientation signal, not a verified regression or improvement.

## Matched comparison: same task id, is the skill itself different too?

**Yes.** `artifacts/v5/seed/` (vendored from this run) is not byte-identical to `artifacts/v4/seed/`
— confirmed by diff: the shared `orchestrator.md` picked up extra icinga-routing guidance between
the two snapshot dates (v4's seed was frozen ~2026-09-20; v5's was copied from the live app on
~2026-10-11). So a `v5_t1_e1` vs. `v4_t4_e1/e2` delta on a matched task reflects the model/gateway
*and* this unrelated skill drift, not a single controlled variable. Read the per-task deltas in
[`cost_time/v5_t1_e1_results_table.md`](cost_time/v5_t1_e1_results_table.md),
[`../../../ui/heatmap_v5_t1_e1.html`](../../../ui/heatmap_v5_t1_e1.html), and
[`../../../reports/v5-vs-v4-h4-comparison.md`](../../../reports/v5-vs-v4-h4-comparison.md) as
orientation, especially where a task's delta is within noise (v4's own e1-vs-e2 repeat swings by
±0.025; h4's by ±0.01).

| matched set | n | prior arm mean | v5_t1_e1 mean | Δ |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| v4-34 (byte-identical task id to v4's 34-task set) | 34 | 0.842 | 0.922 | +0.080 |
| h4-30 (matches an h4 held-out task id) | 21 | 0.724 | 0.915 | +0.191 |
| **both, pooled** | **55** | **0.797** | **0.919** | **+0.122** |

The h4-matched delta (+0.191) is noticeably larger than the v4-matched delta (+0.080) — worth
asking whether that's the harder h4-30 set having more headroom, or something specific to the h4
drop. See the per-category breakdown in `results.json`'s `sections.task.summaries` and the heatmap's
MEAN rows (cloud/cost/icinga/platform) for a finer-grained read; those do not pool v4-34 and h4-30
together.

## Coverage: 2 renamed-but-different, 11 brand new

Two tasks kept their v4/h4 task **number** but got different content, confirmed via diff during
setup (`cost-050-partial-account-coverage`, `cloud-060-marketplace-cost-not-in-usd`) — excluded from
every comparison above, `origin: "renamed-content-changed"` in the ledger. 11 tasks have no v4 or h4
counterpart at all (`origin: "new"`) — see `results.json`'s `task_ledger` for the full list, or any
report under [`../../../reports/v5/v5_t1_e1/`](../../../reports/v5/v5_t1_e1/) tagged `new`.

## Data-quality notes

1. **The skill itself drifted, not just the tasks** — see "Matched comparison" above. This is the
   single most important caveat for anyone reading a per-task delta against v4/h4 as a verified
   result rather than an orientation signal.
2. **`icinga-072-alert-output-not-decoy-metrics` scored a genuine 0.0`** (not an infra error —
   `errored_trials: 0`) — flagged during this session as worth a closer look, not yet investigated.
3. Two genuine setup bugs were found and fixed during this run (broken `_run/skills/` symlinks
   crossing the podman bind-mount boundary; a missing `.env` in the fresh worktree) — both failed
   loudly before any trial ran, so neither could have silently produced a wrong reward. Full
   root-cause detail is in this session's own record, not duplicated here.

## Next moves (open)

- Investigate `icinga-072`'s genuine zero.
- Decide whether to re-run `v5_t1_e1` with a byte-identical `artifacts/v5/seed/` pinned to v4's
  snapshot, to get a controlled A/B before trusting the matched-task deltas above as more than
  orientation.
- Run the audit detectors (`audit_trials.py`, `audit_absence_traps.py`, adapted for v5 in the
  `parsec-intake_v5` worktree, not yet ported here) before treating this arm's numbers as final for
  any decision beyond "the isolated v5 setup runs cleanly."
